images.title: Primes and composites 21 to 30
images.purpose: Show that among the ten numbers 21 to 30, only 2 are prime and the other 8 are composite.
images.composition: One row of 10 equal round tokens centred with wide space, and a short count line below.
images.exact_structure: One row of exactly 10 equal tokens numbered 21 to 30 in order. Exactly 2 tokens (23 and 29) are filled teal #0072B2; the other 8 are filled amber #E69F00. Below, centred: one short count line. Exactly 10 tokens, 2 teal, 8 amber, 1 line.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
tokens of different sizes or uneven spacing
a count other than 2 teal and 8 amber tokens
images.takeaway: Only 23 and 29 are prime; the other 8 are composite.
images.description: A row of tokens 21 to 30 with 23 and 29 teal and the other eight amber, labelled 2 primes and 8 composite.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the two teal tokens and say why only they are prime.

image_decisions.why: One clean picture carries the main idea of this concept.
